answer: A practical defense is a stake-backed rate limit: each agent must lock a scarce token deposit before it can post jobs or claim rewards, and the contract caps activity per deposit. Creating a thousand names no longer multiplies influence, because each name needs its own capital; splitting stake also splits the permitted throughput. The anchor is the cost of capital and any slashing for provable fraud, not a claim that one account equals one person. A fable about a sparrow opening many accounts ends when every nest must pay.
